name: HTML
shortDescription: HTML labels the parts of a web page. Learn to add headings, words, pictures and links. Make your first page with small steps.
highlights: Make a page with headings and words
Build forms and clear page parts

name: CSS
shortDescription: CSS changes how a web page looks. Choose colours, sizes and spaces. Learn to arrange page parts so they fit big and small screens.
highlights: Make pages fit phones and computers

name: Sass
shortDescription: Sass helps you write CSS with reusable names and recipes. A build tool turns your Sass into normal CSS. Start with a colour, then learn to share styles without copying the same lines.
highlights: Practise give a mixin an input

name: Less
shortDescription: Less is a way to write CSS with shared names, small recipes and calculations. A tool turns it into normal CSS. Learn by styling small boxes and checking the CSS that the tool makes.
highlights: Practise store a colour in a name

name: Bootstrap
shortDescription: Bootstrap gives you ready-made page styles. Use short class names to add buttons, cards and columns. Learn HTML and CSS first, then try these steps.
highlights: Arrange a page in rows and columns

name: Tailwind CSS
shortDescription: Tailwind CSS gives small classes one clear style job. You combine the classes to make a page. Start with colours and space, then build cards that fit both narrow and wide screens.
highlights: Practise add inner and outer space

name: JavaScript DOM
shortDescription: The DOM is the browser's model of a page. JavaScript can use it to find a part, change words or react to a click. Learn with small pages that each do one clear job.

name: Web Components
shortDescription: Web Components let you make your own HTML elements with browser tools. A custom element can group a small piece of behaviour and style. Build one greeting first, then learn how it receives values.
highlights: Practise know when an element connects

name: Web Accessibility
shortDescription: An accessible page can be used in different ways. Some people use a keyboard, a screen reader or larger text. Learn small choices that make words, forms and controls easier for more people to use.
highlights: Practise give the page a clear outline
Practise explain a result in words

name: Responsive Web Design
shortDescription: Responsive design makes a page fit the space available. A phone and a large monitor can show the same useful content in different layouts. Learn flexible boxes, readable text and simple screen rules.
highlights: Practise use a flexible content width
Practise make tables usable on narrow screens

name: Progressive Web Apps
shortDescription: A progressive web app is a website that can add useful app features. It may offer an install option or an offline page. Learn how a manifest and a service worker help, without assuming every browser behaves the same.
highlights: Practise describe the app in a manifest
Practise give navigation an offline fallback
Practise save a small local preference

name: Web APIs
shortDescription: A web API is a set of tools the browser offers to JavaScript. Some tools work with text, files or page size. Others ask for permission. Learn a small useful job for each tool and handle cases where it cannot work.
highlights: Practise watch when a part comes into view

name: Web Performance
shortDescription: A fast page lets people read and act without a long wait. Performance work starts with measuring a real task. Learn how images, scripts, styles and layout choices affect the way a page feels.
highlights: Practise know the three web vital ideas
Practise keep early scripts from blocking html
